g.text: Simplest APD = a reverse-biased PIN junction, but:

text.style: font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: • the avalanche width w differs for each carrier

text.style: font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: (it depends on where the photon is absorbed)

text.style: font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: • so a higher field is needed, and breakdown is reached relatively quickly

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Takeaway: avalanche gain multiplies noise by F(M); F stays small only when essentially one carrier ionizes (small k) — Si (k = 0.02) is far quieter than Ge (k = 0.8).

text.style: font-size: 7.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6
